The finite verifier is consistent with the proof but is not used to justify the infinite quantifier.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2025 public source formulates Tian’s fixed-prime conjecture and gives only an at-most-four bound for arbitrary two-prime supports. Targeted published-finding corpus and web searches using the claim, its pure-power-neighbor equivalent forms, and Mersenne/Fermat aliases found no statement that implies the exact support \(\{2,q\}\) classification. Residual risk remains for unindexed folklore or differently phrased work.
residual_risks: An elementary classification may exist in older or unindexed literature under the language of consecutive prime powers, S-unit equations, or triangular numbers.
Search failure is not treated as proof of novelty; acceptance rests on the absence of coverage in the inspected highly relevant current source and the non-implication of the closest returned records.

value.rationale: The result closes a structurally natural fixed-support subfamily of an explicitly current conjecture, improves the cited general two-prime upper bound from four to the conjectured two throughout that family, gives an exact classification, and identifies \(q=3\) as the unique equality case. The role of the unique even prime provides intrinsic mathematical motivation rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
